subject: Dedicated capacity — phased ramp proposal for Acme ML
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood-inference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood-inference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood-inference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft: Acme ML Dedicated prepay + ramp schedule

Team — attaching an initial term sheet for Acme ML. Quick summary: they want a multi-year committed Dedicated pool but will phase their consumption over 18–36 months. My recommended starting point (in the attached v1):
- 3-year prepay (annual invoice) with 22% list discount on committed capacity
- Ramp schedule (committed GPUs / TPM equivalent): Y1 = 25%, Y2 = 50%, Y3 = 100%
- Flex buffer: 10% credits in year 1 to accommodate delayed ramp (non-refundable if unused)
- True-up at each anniversary; failure-to-ramp triggers true-up, not cash penalties (suggest legal review)

Questions for pricing/legal:
1) Can we offer a stronger discount (25%) if they accept a minimum ARR threshold across 3 years?
2) Do we allow invoice cadence to be annual prepay only (helps cash), or can we support annual invoice with monthly usage reporting/true-ups?
3) How tight should the failure-to-ramp language be? Legal prefers true-up vs clawback; product/ops want a minimal buffer for capacity scheduling.

Attach: Dedicated_Term_Sheet_AcmeML_v1.pdf (stub)

— Lauren Bishop
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood-inference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood-inference.com>
To: Sofia Muñoz <sofia.mu@acme-ml.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acme-ml.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood Dedicated proposal — phased ramp & term pricing

Hi Sofia — great conversation last week. As discussed, attached is a proposed term sheet for a Dedicated prepay with a phased ramp to match your project milestones. High level:

- Option (3-year prepay): 22% discount on list price across committed capacity; annual invoice (prepay).
- Proposed ramp (baseline): Year 1 = 25% of committed GPUs, Year 2 = 50%, Year 3 = 100%.
- Flex credits: 10% buffer applied in Year 1 to offset delayed onboarding; unused credits expire at year-end.
- True-up: annual true-up at each anniversary to reconcile actual usage vs committed capacity.
- SLA & support: 99.9% uptime SLA + priority onboarding; SOC 2 Type II available on request.

Next steps I propose:
1) Procurement confirms preferred ramp shape and billing cadence (annual prepay vs quarterly).
2) If OK, we issue v2 term sheet and a short MOU via DocuSign to lock in pricing while legal reviews the master services agreement.

I've attached the term sheet (v1). Happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk through.

Attachments: Dedicated_Term_Sheet_AcmeML_v1.pdf

Best,
Lauren
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Sofia Muñoz <sofia.mu@acme-ml.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acme-ml.com>, Cloud Ops <cloud-ops@acme-ml.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood Dedicated proposal — phased ramp & term pricing

Hi Lauren — thanks for the proposal. A few questions/requests from procurement and cloud ops:

- Ramp: Our program budget phases mean we cannot hit 25% in Y1. Proposed ramp we need: Y1 = 10%, Y2 = 40%, Y3 = 50%. Can you accommodate that?
- Discount: If we move to multi-year prepay, we would need a stronger commercial incentive. Can you go to ~25% off list for a 3-year prepay (or provide additional service credits)?
- Failure-to-ramp: Procurement dislikes hard cash true-ups. Can you offer a softer true-up (e.g., crediting future invoices or a rollover for a limited period) rather than immediate invoiced true-ups?
- Billing cadence: We prefer annual prepay invoiced upfront to match our budget cycle; however, we need monthly usage statements for internal showback.
- Legal/Security: please attach SOC2 and if possible a short SLA addendum and data egress terms.

We need to get commercialization approval internally (procurement + finance) — if you can provide a revised term sheet with the ramp variant and an improved discount/credit structure, we can move to MOU stage quickly. Also please include HubSpot deal ID for our reference in the MOU.

Thanks — Sofia
Sofia Muñoz
Head of Cloud Engineering, Acme ML
sofia.mu@acme-ml.com
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood-inference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood-inference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood-inference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Re: Redwood Dedicated proposal — phased ramp & term pricing

Forwarding Sofia's reply — key asks: shallower Y1 ramp, stronger commercial, softer true-up semantics, annual prepay invoice + monthly usage reporting.

My thoughts:
- Commercial: willing to consider 25% discount if we can get a minimum 3-year ARR threshold (e.g., commit to X TPM or $Y total). That removes churn risk.
- Ramp: they want Y1=10% Y2=40% Y3=50% — operationally we can schedule capacity assuming they provide reasonable forecast windows.
- True-up: product/ops prefer annual true-up invoiced vs credits; procurement prefers credits/rollover. Can we compromise: annual true-up but allow a one-year rollover of up to 25% of missed ramp as credits?

Action items: Rishi — confirm if pricing can stretch to 25% with a minimum ARR gate and what that gate looks like in TPM/GPU terms. Neha — run the failure-to-ramp clause language with legal; prefer to avoid clawbacks in the MOU. Marcus — confirm whether we can reserve capacity with a flexible buffer for Y1.

HubSpot reference: HS-98765 (include in MOU)
Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0Bxyz

— Lauren
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood-inference.com>
To: Sofia Muñoz <sofia.mu@acme-ml.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acme-ml.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood-inference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood-inference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Revised proposal — two options for Acme ML (v2)

Hi Sofia — thanks for the clarity. Per internal alignment, please find two options below (v2 term sheet attached):

Option A — 3-year (recommended)
- Discount: 22% base, bumped to 25% if Acme commits to minimum 3-year ARR of $2.1M (equivalent GPU/TPM schedule detailed in the sheet).
- Ramp: Y1 = 15%, Y2 = 35%, Y3 = 50% (compromise between your ask and operational predictability).
- Flex credits: Up to 25% of missed ramp can be rolled forward as credits once during the term (must be used within next 12 months).
- True-up: Annual true-up at anniversary; if usage < committed, credits roll as above instead of cash clawback.
- Billing: Annual prepay invoice (preferred) with monthly usage statements for showback.

Option B — 2-year (accelerated)
- Discount: 18%
- Ramp: Y1 = 50% Y2 = 100%
- Less flex; stricter true-up (annual, invoiced).

Attachments: Dedicated_Term_Sheet_AcmeML_v2.pdf (includes SLA addendum and SOC2 link)
DocuSign: https://www.docusign.net/initial-mou/ABC123 (MOU for Option A enclosed)

If Option A is acceptable, we'll issue an MOU (DocuSign) capturing the 25% conditional discount clause and the rollover credit language, then proceed to legal for the full MSA. If you'd like to discuss, I'm available tomorrow morning for a 30-min call.

Best,
Lauren
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Sofia Muñoz <sofia.mu@acme-ml.com>

Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Revised proposal — two options for Acme ML (v2)

Lauren — thanks, Option A looks workable to commercialization and procurement on a provisional basis. Two quick asks before we send to legal:
1) Please put the minimum ARR threshold ($2.1M) explicitly in the MOU and note that the discount becomes effective upon MOU signature and first invoice payment.
2) Confirm the rollover credit mechanics in plain language (we need a short paragraph for procurement).

If you can update the MOU with those clarifications, procurement will start the redline process this afternoon and we can schedule a kickoff next week with Cloud Ops. Please include HS-98765 in the MOU header.

CCing Procurement and Cloud Ops to keep them in the loop.

Best,
Sofia
